import { useState } from "react";

import { useTypedEventEmitter } from "../../hooks/useEventEmitter";
import { MatrixClientPeg } from "../../MatrixClientPeg";
import { VoiceBroadcastPlayback, VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent, VoiceBroadcastPlaybackState } from "..";

export const useVoiceBroadcastPlayback = (playback: VoiceBroadcastPlayback) => {
    const client = MatrixClientPeg.get();
    const room = client.getRoom(playback.infoEvent.getRoomId());

    if (!room) {
        throw new Error(`Voice Broadcast room not found (event ${playback.infoEvent.getId()})`);
    }

    const playbackToggle = () => {
        playback.toggle();
    };

    const [playbackState, setPlaybackState] = useState(playback.getState());
    useTypedEventEmitter(
        playback,
        VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent.StateChanged,
        (state: VoiceBroadcastPlaybackState, _playback: VoiceBroadcastPlayback) => {
            setPlaybackState(state);
        },
    );

    const [times, setTimes] = useState({
        duration: playback.durationSeconds,
        position: playback.timeSeconds,
        timeLeft: playback.timeLeftSeconds,
    });
    useTypedEventEmitter(playback, VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent.TimesChanged, (t) => setTimes(t));

    const [liveness, setLiveness] = useState(playback.getLiveness());
    useTypedEventEmitter(playback, VoiceBroadcastPlaybackEvent.LivenessChanged, (l) => setLiveness(l));

    return {
        times,
        liveness: liveness,
        playbackState,
        room: room,
        sender: playback.infoEvent.sender,
        toggle: playbackToggle,
    };
};

item.text: The mismatch is in `VoiceBroadcastPlayback.updateLiveness()`: it also checks playback state and whether the current chunk is last. That can make a Started or Resumed broadcast appear grey even though its info state says it is live. I’m checking the existing tests and state transition paths for the full impact.

item.text:
I found the cause in [VoiceBroadcastPlayback.ts](/app/src/voice-broadcast/models/VoiceBroadcastPlayback.ts:323). `updateLiveness()` uses playback state and the current chunk as well as info state, so a Started or Resumed broadcast can appear grey while playback is stopped, paused, or buffering. `setState()`, `skipTo()`, and first-chunk handling can also change liveness independently of `setInfoState()`.

The fix should put the requested mapping in `determineVoiceBroadcastLiveness.ts` and have `setInfoState()` alone apply it through `setLiveness()`. The existing `setLiveness()` guard already prevents duplicate change events. Invalid incoming info states are currently ignored, so whether those events should reset liveness remains an ambiguity; the utility itself should return `not-live` for unknown or undefined input.

The existing model suite passes (40/40), but [its Resumed-without-chunks test](/app/test/voice-broadcast/models/VoiceBroadcastPlayback-test.ts:193) expects the old grey behavior. **No project source or tests were edited**: this pass was limited to fault localization. Findings are recorded in [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md).
